name: Luciano Benetton
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (1996-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Luciano Benetton started the Benetton Group in 1965 with his three siblings, Carlo (d.2018), Gilberto (d.2018) and Giuliana.
Known for their colorful sweaters, Benetton won over parts of the world, opening its first store in Paris in 1969 and reaching New York in 1980.
In 2018, 12 years after leaving and allowing outside managers to take on greater roles, Luciano returned to help turn the company around.
The family has invested in Italian businesses including Mundys, a highway infrastructure company that accounts for more than half their fortune.
forbes_facts: Luciano was elected to the Italian Senate in 1992 and served until 1994.
At age 14 Luciano's father died. Soon after he started working at a clothing store to help his family make ends meet.

name: Margaret Baker
forbes_bio: Margaret "Peggy" Baker is a shareholder of Illinois-based medical supplies giant Medline, which her father Jim Mills and uncle Jon Mills founded in 1966.

The extended Mills family, which includes four other billionaires, owns roughly 18% of the company, which IPO'd on the Nasdaq in December 2025 and ended its first trading day with a market cap of more than $55 billion.
The Mills family previously sold 79% of Medline to a group of private equity firms in a leveraged buyout that valued the company at more than $30 billion in 2021.

Baker's brother Charlie Mills served as Medline's CEO for 26 years until 2023, while her cousin Andy Mills served as president during that same period. Charlie still serves as chairman and Andy still sits on the board.
Andy Mills' brother-in-law Jim Abrams served as chief operating officer of Medline from 1997 to 2023. The company is now run by non-family executives.

name: Fu Liquan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: Fu Liquan is the chairman of Zhejiang Dahua Technology, one of China's biggest surveillance businesses.
Fu worked at a small electrical equipment factory before starting his first equipment plant in 1993.
Fu's wife Chen Ailing sits on Dahua's board of directors.
forbes_facts: One of Fu's favorite books is Winning by Jack Welch.

name: Vanessa Hartono
forbes_bio: Vanessa Hartono inherited her wealth from her late father Michael "Bambang" Hartono.
Michael was among the richest in Indonesia and owned a stake in Bank Central Asia together with his brother R. Budi. Michael died in March 2026 at age 86.
The Hartonos bought the stake in BCA after another wealthy family, the Salims, lost control of the bank during the 1997-1998 Asian economic crisis.
The family first got rich in tobacco and is still one of the biggest clove cigarette makers in the nation.

Family holdings also include prime real estate in Jakarta and popular electronics brand Polytron, which forayed into the EV business on its home turf in 2025 with the launch of two electric car models.
forbes_facts: In what was Indonesia's second-largest IPO of 2022, the Hartonos listed Global Digital Niaga, which owns e-commerce giant Blibli, raising $510 million.

name: Shi Yuzhu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2004-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: Shi Yuzhu is chairman of Giant Interactive, an online game developer and operator in China.
Giant, which had traded in New York, was relisted on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2016 through a reverse merger with Chongqing New Century Cruise.
Shi was a revered entrepreneur in China in the 1980s when he first made his fortune in computer hardware.
A graduate of Zhejiang University, Shi got his degree in math.

name: Huijiao Yu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2014-2026); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Yu Huijiao chairs Shanghai-listed YTO Express Group, one of China's largest express delivery firms.
Sixteen years ago unpaid customer bills left Yu Huijiao's architectural firm bankrupt; it took a decade to pay back creditors.
During that period, Yu decided to start his delivery business with help from his wife, Zhang Xiaoyuan.

name: Ion Tiriac
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Ion Tiriac is a former professional athlete who heads Tiriac Group, which has interests in real estate, auto, financial services and more.
After he retired as a tennis player in the 1970s, Tiriac coached and managed top players like Guillermo Vilas, Marat Safin and Boris Becker.
He began his investment career after the fall of communism in Romania, and eventually founded the Tiriac Group.
He owns a car and motorcycle collection of more than 400 models, including cars previously owned by Al Capone, Sammy Davis Jr. and Elton John.
Tiriac has also represented Romania internationally in ice hockey, including an appearance in the 1964 Winter Olympics and three Davis Cup finals.
forbes_facts: Known as Count Dracula in his tennis years, Tiriac is one of the richest former athletes of all time.
He formed a formidable doubles team with Ilie Nastase and captured a Grand Slam doubles title and a runners-up finish as well.

name: Sharon Azrieli
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Sharon Azrieli is an heir to the Azrieli Group real estate fortune.
She and her two sisters, Danna and Naomi Azrieli, own about 46% of the publicly traded company.
She sits on the board and inherited her stake after her father, David Azrieli, died in 2014.
Sharon is also on the board of the family's Azrieli Foundation, which supports a number of causes, including science, music and Holocaust education.

name: Michael Patterson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Patterson is a founding partner of HPS Investment Partners, one of the world's biggest alternative credit managers with $149 billion in assets.
He oversees HPS' specialty lending, corporate lending and core senior lending funds, and previously worked at Silver Point Capital and Goldman Sachs.
HPS was sold to BlackRock in July 2025 for around $12 billion in BlackRock stock.
Prior to his investing career, he served as an officer in the United States Navy. He serves on the Dean's Advisory Council for the Radcliffe Institute of Advanced Studies at Harvard.
Patterson holds an AB in Applied Mathematics from Harvard College and an MBA from Stanford.

name: Yoshiko Mori
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Yoshiko Mori is the widow of real estate tycoon Minoru Mori, who died in 2012.
She inherited part of Minoru's estate, including a share of his real estate firm, Mori Building.
Mori Building is known for developments such as Tokyo's swank Roppongi Hills complex, a mix of retail, restaurants, apartments, hotel and offices.
Mori Building also co-developed one of China's tallest buildings, the Shanghai World Financial Center.
In 2023, it opened its largest project in two decades, the $4.3 billion Azabudai Hills in Tokyo, an office, condo, retail and hotel complex, including Japan's tallest building at 330 meters.
